module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 244

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos244

/-- Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_244 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ C > (1 : ℝ), 0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/-- Romanoff [Ro34] proved that the answer is yes if $C$ is an integer.

[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., _Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie_.
Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_244.variants.Romanoff {C : ℕ} (hC : 1 < C) :
    0 < { p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ | (p) (k) (_ : p.Prime) }.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos244

review.notes:
Both Erdos244.erdos_244 and Erdos244.erdos_244.variants.Romanoff faithfully state their respective claims. Ding explicitly identifies the question as positive lower asymptotic density for every real base greater than 1; his almost-everywhere result does not settle the general question.

Lean experiments in /workspace/review/experiments.lean compile successfully. They confirm the inferred natural-number domains of p and k, inclusion of k = 0, agreement of natural and integer floors on the permitted inputs, and the integer-base specialization. They also verify boundary cases and prove that positive lowerDensity is equivalent to an eventual positive linear lower bound on the counting function. The zero denominator at the initial counting index and the infinite-set default of Set.ncard do not affect these statements.

The live erdosproblems.com page was Cloudflare-blocked; its archived text was read and corroborated by Ding’s recent paper and the current community status database.
